title: Spatial Report — 2026-06-26

HIGHLIGHTS.title: OpenAI will delay GPT-5.6 after Trump administration request
HIGHLIGHTS.summary: The Verge reports that OpenAI will delay the full release of GPT-5.6 after the Trump administration, citing potential security concerns, asked the company to stagger its rollout. The Information first reported that CEO Sam Altman told employees in a company Q&A that GPT-5.6 will initially launch in limited preview form to a small group, marking a notable instance of federal influence over a frontier model release schedule.

APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS.title: Apple Vision Pro’s longest immersive concert was harder to film than you’d think
APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS.summary: CineD interviewed director Ian Russell about producing Debut at the BBC Proms for Apple Vision Pro, including the use of five Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive cameras, new framing and camera-placement constraints, and the shift from conventional concert production to stereoscopic 180-degree filming.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: OpenAI's free GPT-5.5 model makes ChatGPT better at understanding context
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Engadget reports that OpenAI has rolled out GPT-5.5, a free upgrade to the default ChatGPT model, with improvements aimed at better context understanding for the company's most widely used tier of users.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: I Met With China’s Top AI Experts. They’re Freaking Out, Too
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: Wired reports that researchers on both sides of the US–China AI race are increasingly worried about a potential 'Chernobyl moment,' with top Chinese AI experts the publication met expressing concern about the speed and competitive intensity of frontier model development.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.title: OpenAI reveals its first AI processor: Jalapeño
AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS.summary: The Verge reports that OpenAI has unveiled its first in-house AI chip, called Jalapeño, an application-specific integrated circuit designed for AI inference and built in partnership with Broadcom, marking the company's move into custom silicon for current and future large language models.

RESEARCH.title: ARTOO-DARTU: Studying AR-HRC With AR Obstruction Mitigation During a Warehouse Task
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv paper titled ARTOO-DARTU studies augmented reality human-robot collaboration during a warehouse task, examining how AR situated analytics can obstruct important real-world elements when content is dynamically positioned relative to mobile robots, and proposing obstruction mitigation techniques to improve safety and usability.

RESEARCH.title: Co-designing a Preliminary Repository of Augmented Reality Concepts for Real-Time Emotion Regulation
RESEARCH.summary: Researchers on arXiv present a co-designed preliminary repository of augmented reality concepts for real-time emotion regulation, addressing the lack of user-centered, expert-informed design resources for AR-based mental health support that does not disengage users from their ongoing activities.

RESEARCH.title: Dissociable Spatial and Temporal Effects of Interaction Latency in Virtual Reality
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv study investigates dissociable spatial and temporal effects of interaction latency in virtual reality, examining how motion-to-photon latency from head movement and hand-to-virtual-effector loops impair VR performance and whether common spatial, temporal, and efficiency measures capture latency effects equivalently.

RESEARCH.title: Virtual Reality Alters Perceived Functional Body Size
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv study with 60 participants finds that immersive virtual reality presented through a head-mounted display alters perceived functional body size, using a passable aperture paradigm to compare action and perception tasks across physical and VR conditions.

RESEARCH.title: From Sparse and Imperfect 2D Anchors to Consistent 3D Gaussian Street Scenes: Support-Aware Appearance
RESEARCH.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a support-aware appearance method for building consistent 3D Gaussian street scenes from sparse and imperfect 2D anchors, using teacher-relative appearance residual distillation to handle view-specific noise and enable standard-rasterizer deployment.

RESEARCH.title: SplatPainter: Interactive Authoring of 3D Gaussians from 2D Edits via Test-Time Training
RESEARCH.summary: A paper posted to arXiv introduces SplatPainter, a method for interactively editing 3D Gaussian Splatting assets by propagating 2D edits into the underlying 3D representation via test-time training, addressing limitations of diffusion- and optimization-based approaches that the authors describe as slow, destructive to asset identity, or lacking fine-grained control.

RESEARCH.title: StayStill: a large-scale 3D idle animation dataset
RESEARCH.summary: A new arXiv paper introduces StayStill, a large-scale 3D idle animation dataset comprising approximately six hours of motion data captured from 50 subjects, aimed at filling a gap in training data for automatic generation of realistic inactive-state behaviors in virtual characters. The authors argue that idle motion has received limited attention compared to other animation tasks despite its importance for believable avatars in XR and gaming contexts.

items.summary: A paper posted to arXiv introduces SplatPainter, a method for interactively editing 3D Gaussian Splatting assets by propagating 2D edits into the underlying 3D representation via test-time training, addressing limitations of diffusion- and optimization-based approaches that the authors describe as slow, destructive to asset identity, or lacking fine-grained control.

items.title: StayStill: a large-scale 3D idle animation dataset

Spatial Report
Week of 2026-06-26

HIGHLIGHTS

The Verge reports that OpenAI will delay the full release of GPT-5.6 after the Trump administration, citing potential security concerns, asked the company to stagger its rollout. The Information first reported that CEO Sam Altman told employees in a company Q&A that GPT-5.6 will initially launch in limited preview form to a small group, marking a notable instance of federal influence over a frontier model release schedule.

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/957372/openai-will-delay-gpt-5-6-after-trump-administration-request

APP STORE HIGHLIGHTS

CineD interviewed director Ian Russell about producing Debut at the BBC Proms for Apple Vision Pro, including the use of five Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive cameras, new framing and camera-placement constraints, and the shift from conventional concert production to stereoscopic 180-degree filming.

AI AND SIMULATED WORLDS

Engadget reports that OpenAI has rolled out GPT-5.5, a free upgrade to the default ChatGPT model, with improvements aimed at better context understanding for the company's most widely used tier of users.

https://www.engadget.com/2201255/openai-gpt-5-5-instant-chatgpt-upgrade/

Wired reports that researchers on both sides of the US–China AI race are increasingly worried about a potential 'Chernobyl moment,' with top Chinese AI experts the publication met expressing concern about the speed and competitive intensity of frontier model development.

https://www.wired.com/story/ai-arms-race-china-us-cooperation/

The Verge reports that OpenAI has unveiled its first in-house AI chip, called Jalapeño, an application-specific integrated circuit designed for AI inference and built in partnership with Broadcom, marking the company's move into custom silicon for current and future large language models.

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/955939/openai-reveals-its-first-ai-processor-jalapeno

RESEARCH

An arXiv paper titled ARTOO-DARTU studies augmented reality human-robot collaboration during a warehouse task, examining how AR situated analytics can obstruct important real-world elements when content is dynamically positioned relative to mobile robots, and proposing obstruction mitigation techniques to improve safety and usability.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25202

Researchers on arXiv present a co-designed preliminary repository of augmented reality concepts for real-time emotion regulation, addressing the lack of user-centered, expert-informed design resources for AR-based mental health support that does not disengage users from their ongoing activities.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25271

An arXiv study investigates dissociable spatial and temporal effects of interaction latency in virtual reality, examining how motion-to-photon latency from head movement and hand-to-virtual-effector loops impair VR performance and whether common spatial, temporal, and efficiency measures capture latency effects equivalently.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25681

An arXiv study with 60 participants finds that immersive virtual reality presented through a head-mounted display alters perceived functional body size, using a passable aperture paradigm to compare action and perception tasks across physical and VR conditions.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00824

An arXiv paper introduces a support-aware appearance method for building consistent 3D Gaussian street scenes from sparse and imperfect 2D anchors, using teacher-relative appearance residual distillation to handle view-specific noise and enable standard-rasterizer deployment.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26007

A paper posted to arXiv introduces SplatPainter, a method for interactively editing 3D Gaussian Splatting assets by propagating 2D edits into the underlying 3D representation via test-time training, addressing limitations of diffusion- and optimization-based approaches that the authors describe as slow, destructive to asset identity, or lacking fine-grained control.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05354

A new arXiv paper introduces StayStill, a large-scale 3D idle animation dataset comprising approximately six hours of motion data captured from 50 subjects, aimed at filling a gap in training data for automatic generation of realistic inactive-state behaviors in virtual characters. The authors argue that idle motion has received limited attention compared to other animation tasks despite its importance for believable avatars in XR and gaming contexts.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13693
